fatal_errors: The proposed dropwise, inert-atmosphere synthesis at 100–150°C does not reconstruct the spray-drying followed by H2 reduction at 300°C used in the target work.
The central target mechanism—early Pt, Ir, or Ru reduction, noble-metal-mediated H2 dissociation and hydrogen-assisted reduction of neighboring transition metals, with Pd failing—is absent.

The controlled comparison changes the number and identity of metals rather than directly varying precursor mobility, so it cannot uniquely attribute either homogeneity or catalytic performance to mobility suppression.
Catalytic predictions use an unspecified model reaction and binary-alloy baseline rather than methanol oxidation against commercial Pt black.
The asserted isolated active-site mechanism is not established by the cited evidence and is not directly tested by the proposed characterization.
explanation: The response addresses the broad problem of kinetic control over noble-metal HEA formation and offers a scientifically plausible alternative supported by relevant literature. E1 supports reduction-kinetic control under dropwise precursor addition, and E2 supports stochastic single-phase formation when many atom types have limited mobility. However, it largely reconstructs those cited studies rather than the hidden target. It misses the SD-TDR process, H2 atmosphere, 300°C reduction, porous 3D nanoframework morphology, Pt/Ir/Ru-specific hydrogen activation, Pd and noble-metal-free controls, Pt–Ru fcc-to-hcp transformation, and methanol-oxidation results. Its temperature and atmosphere boundaries are asserted without support from the supplied evidence. Most importantly, the proposed five-metal-versus-binary experiment does not independently perturb mobility, and catalytic differences would be confounded by composition, surface area, and active-metal identity. A discriminating test would compare the same composition under low- and high-mobility synthesis conditions, while separately benchmarking MOR against Pt black and measuring phase purity, elemental homogeneity, and electrochemically active surface area.
